title: Fix delegated admin token scope synchronization and missing audit entries
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: A customer escalated that a user with a read-only role briefly observed admin-level UI controls after an SSO invite+link flow. Investigation shows a two-part bug: (1) delegated admin tokens can be minted with ephemeral role identifiers that aren't canonicalized against the RBAC canonical_role table, and (2) the audit ingestion pipeline filtered out events with the transient_scope flag, so the grant event was not visible in audit logs. Together these produced a silent overgrant and missing audit entries. This ticket implements fixes, tests, and a short remediation path for recent customers.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure SAML group sync with nested groups and a delegated admin connector.
2) Invite user X via SSO with 'Invite + Link' flow while group sync is running.
3) During group sync fold, trigger a role mapping refresh (simulate group membership change).
4) Immediately perform an action requiring admin-level permission; observe access granted intermittently.
5) Check audit logs for the equivalent grant event; initial pipeline shows no matching audit entry for the overgrant.
root_cause: Race between role_mapping cache eviction and delegated-token mint path produced tokens carrying ephemeral role IDs (role_ref:<uuid-temp>) rather than canonical_role_id:<uuid>. Audit ingestion applies strict canonical_role filter and transient_scope events were dropped. Additionally, role_merge ordering between SAML nested groups was non-deterministic which widened the window where a transient mapping could be used to compute effective permissions at token mint time.
impact_summary: High risk for customer security posture: potential temporary privilege escalation without auditable evidence. Affected customers are those using delegated connectors + SAML group-sync within high churn orgs. We observed 3 escalations in the last 30 days; one customer flagged a potential compliance violation.
mitigation_implemented: Hotfix: force canonical_role lookup during token mint (deployed as runtime patch v1.2.3-hotfix on 2026-02-28).
Temporary mitigation: added a short-lived guard that rejects delegated-token minting when role_mapping cache reports 'stale' (rolled to prod 2026-03-03).
Customer outreach: notified affected accounts and provided manual audit exports where possible.
proposed_fix: 1) Ensure token mint path canonicalizes all role references to canonical_role_id at mint time and stores canonical ids in token metadata. 2) Update audit ingestion to enrich transient events by resolving ephemeral role_refs to canonical_role_ids using the same resolver used in mint. 3) Make SAML group-merge ordering deterministic (sort by external_group_id then depth) to reduce race window. 4) Add unit/integration tests covering group sync churn + token mint race.
implementation_notes: Change touches: auth/token-service (mint flow), rbac/canonicalizer, audit/ingest, saml/group-sync merge logic.
Key kernel: do canonical lookup under a short transaction to avoid TOCTOU where possible, fallback to synchronous resolver call if cache misses.
Avoid heavy blocking on mint path: canonicalization must be low-latency; we cache canonical ids with write-through invalidation on group-sync events.
testing_plan: Add chaos test in staging that simulates group-sync churn and concurrent token mints (integration tests).
Add unit tests for canonicalizer with ephemeral -> canonical mapping cases.
Run full CI and a targeted performance benchmark to assert mint latency < 50ms with canonicalization enabled.
rollout_plan: Canary patch to 10% of runtime pool for 48 hours, monitor auth-success-rate, error rate, and token-mint latency. If stable, increase to 50% for 24 hours, then full rollout. Coordinate with on-call and CSMs for affected customers to observe for regressions.
downgrade_plan: Rollback runtime change and revert to previous token-service binary if token-mint latency regressions or new authorization failures exceed threshold. Restore temporary 'reject when stale' guard if needed.
observability_and_alerting: New audit-lag metric for enriched events.
Alert: >1% increase in auth-deny for previously allowed flows (5m window).
